evidence.exact_quote: - Consumer docs must not mix canonical blocked/scheduler/remediation lineage with legacy tier-event push streams.

items.impact: Consumers can comply differently because coexistence, rejection, and completion criteria for legacy tier-event demotion are not defined here.
items.statement: AI-039 forbids mixing canonical remediation lineage with legacy tier-event streams, but does not specify an executable migration oracle or invalid mixed-state handling.
items.title: Legacy event demotion lacks a closure oracle

evidence.exact_quote: - Runtime/chat boundaries must avoid over-unify and under-unify behavior.

items.impact: Owner and consumer repairs can settle on incompatible boundaries without a falsifiable test for over-unification or under-unification.
items.statement: AI-040 establishes owner-first repair ordering, but leaves the runtime/chat boundary acceptance test undefined.
items.title: Runtime chat boundary is not falsifiable

evidence.exact_quote: - Puppet Master MUST remain one extensible platform, not separate hard-forked products or rigid personalities.

items.impact: Activation UIs and services may record, default, or override ambiguous interpretations inconsistently.
items.statement: AI-041 requires visible and overridable project ambiguity, but does not define ambiguity-state schema, default-selection authority, or override persistence.
items.title: Project ambiguity lifecycle is unspecified

evidence.exact_quote: - Affected features must not pretend full readiness while indexes or external model/capability reports are still synchronizing.

items.impact: Surfaces may disclose degraded operation but disagree on readiness thresholds, failure transitions, retry, and offline behavior.
items.statement: AI-042 prohibits false readiness during synchronization, yet defines no shared degraded/readiness state machine or recovery contract.
items.title: Degraded readiness has no state machine

evidence.exact_quote: - Module activation must not create unbounded startup work, hidden dependency chains, or duplicate project-detection logic.

items.impact: Backend/helper mismatches or interrupted lazy activation can leave remote projects in unrecoverable or misleading states.
items.statement: AI-043 constrains startup and dependency breadth, but omits remote attachment version negotiation, partial activation cleanup, and rollback behavior.
items.title: Remote activation recovery is undefined

evidence.exact_quote: - Addressing cannot assume rigid <phase>/<task>/<subtask> paths when package/seam architecture is active.

items.impact: Reconciliation can claim dependency-driven order without machine-checkable dependencies, cycle detection, or completion gates.
items.statement: AI-044 mandates dependency-driven seam order and package/seam addressing, but the PlanUnit encodes no dependencies or ordering oracle.
items.title: Seam reconciliation order is not encoded

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Puppet Master keeps a PM-native Rust plus Slint service-bound workbench architecture, preserving benchmark/research
- Rust/Tauri

items.impact: A builder may incorrectly interpret Tauri as part of the current foundation rather than bounded research lineage.
items.statement: AI-045 names Rust plus Slint as the native workbench architecture while retaining Rust/Tauri as an undispositioned exact token, leaving lineage interpretation ambiguous.
items.title: Rust Tauri lineage can mislead builders

evidence.exact_quote: coalesced background projections with explicit revalidation before mutation.
- Git/SCM subprocess work is never an editor or UI hot-path dependency.

items.impact: A projection can become stale between revalidation and mutation, allowing TOCTOU races or inconsistent retries.
items.statement: AI-046 separates UI hot paths from background services but does not define projection versions, freshness budgets, or atomic revalidation-and-mutate semantics.
items.title: Projection revalidation is race-prone

evidence.exact_quote: - OS-facing behavior must not be implemented as scattered per-view shortcuts.

items.impact: Platform-specific failures, unsupported capabilities, and accessibility bridge degradation can surface inconsistently.
items.statement: AI-047 centralizes OS behavior behind platform adapters, but does not define capability negotiation, unsupported-operation results, or fallback behavior.
items.title: Platform adapter failures lack a contract

evidence.exact_quote: - The shared Rust core owns cross-surface core services while platform adapters own OS specifics.

items.impact: The explicit split prevents views, paths, and platform adapters from silently re-owning core state.
items.statement: AI-048 gives the shared Rust core a concrete cross-surface ownership inventory and cleanly separates OS-specific adapter authority.
items.title: Shared core ownership is explicit

evidence.exact_quote:
- File watchers, remote file-change notifications, and provider update streams are invalidation signals, not authoritative
  state.

items.impact: Bursts, reordering, dropped notifications, and offline recovery can produce stale visibility across tree, search, LSP, SCM, and preview surfaces.
items.statement: AI-049 correctly demotes watchers and provider streams to invalidation signals, but omits ordering, coalescing, reconciliation, and stale-projection recovery semantics.
items.title: Invalidation signals lack reconciliation semantics

evidence.exact_quote: - External engines and CLIs may be reused only as adapters inside PM-owned boundaries.

items.impact: The rule blocks delegated core ownership and browser-specific assumptions from becoming native architectural dependencies.
items.statement: AI-050 clearly constrains external engines and CLIs to PM-owned adapter seams and rejects browser-first architectural foundations.
items.title: External adapter authority is bounded

evidence.exact_quote:
- Debug/investigation flows MUST record typed budget exhaustion rather than collapsing every stop into a generic failure or
  blocked state.

items.impact: Retry, resume, cleanup, and attention flows may interpret the same budget exhaustion differently or lose terminal-state legality.
items.statement: AI-051 requires typed budget exhaustion but does not map each budget kind to legal lifecycle transitions, retry authority, cleanup, or terminal outcomes.
items.title: Typed exhaustion lacks transition semantics

evidence.exact_quote: - max_verification_attempts_per_fix_candidate = 2
- max_package_or_tool_installs = 2

items.impact: Builders must invent ceilings, units, reset scopes, and enforcement behavior for the remaining budget kinds.
items.statement: AI-052 enumerates fourteen budget kinds but supplies MVP ceilings for only two and leaves the rest without default or required configuration semantics.
items.title: Investigation budget defaults are incomplete

evidence.exact_quote:
canonical_text: Only package or tool installs that persist beyond a single process lifetime count against max_package_or_tool_installs;
  ephemeral per-process installs may be logged as investigation context but do not consume the install budget.

items.impact: Repeated, upgraded, rolled-back, cached, or shared installs may be counted inconsistently and bypass or prematurely exhaust the budget.
items.statement: AI-053 distinguishes persistent from ephemeral installs, but does not define install identity, process lifetime scope, reinstall counting, or rollback effects.
items.title: Install budget accounting is ambiguous

evidence.exact_quote: - Debug Mode MUST preserve evidence planes instead of collapsing them into one owner model.

items.impact: Evidence crossing planes may inherit the wrong trust, redaction, retention, or authority semantics.
items.statement: AI-054 preserves distinct debug evidence planes but does not define permitted cross-plane references, transformations, trust changes, or lifecycle controls.
items.title: Debug evidence planes lack crossing rules

evidence.exact_quote: - Debug Mode must not become a new execution-posture enum.
- Deep Plan does not create a sub-task inheritance path or widen child authority.

items.impact: The explicit split prevents a user-visible workflow mode from silently changing execution posture or delegated authority.
items.statement: AI-055 explicitly bounds Debug as a chat/workflow overlay and Deep Plan as single-threaded read-only planning without child-authority inheritance.
items.title: Debug and Deep Plan authority is bounded

evidence.exact_quote: - Remote target, capability, storage, prompt, permission, and browser evidence seams require explicit owners.

items.impact: MVP authority can still be inferred from labels because no accountable owner or interface is bound to each required seam here.
items.statement: AI-056 says seven Debug MVP seams require explicit owners but does not name those owners or their contract entry points.
items.title: Debug MVP seams have no named owners

evidence.exact_quote:
canonical_text: Browser evidence auto-feed must be a visible attach /bundle contract and must not contradict the no hidden
  browser-to-chat injection rule; bounded auto-feed is allowed only through visible Investigation Context state, consented
  attach/revoke affordances, and owner-routed browser capture events.

items.impact: Users may revoke evidence visually while copies remain active in prompts, bundles, exports, caches, or downstream consumers.
items.statement: AI-057 requires visible consented attach/revoke, but does not define revocation propagation, derived-copy deletion, partial attach failure, or UI confirmation semantics.
items.title: Browser evidence revocation is incomplete

evidence.exact_quote:
canonical_text: In-scope tool-emitted evidence for an active investigation enters Investigation Context as active unless redaction,
  trust, or /truncation policy narrows it; out-of-scope evidence remains referenced or rejected instead of silently injected.
  Exported or replayed Debug verification evidence carries heuristic_version = debug_verify.v1, and future debug_verify tuning
  increments or preserves heuristic_version.

items.impact: Implementations can disagree on precedence, state transitions, retention, and replay trust for sensitive or truncated evidence.
items.statement: AI-058 names active, referenced, and rejected outcomes plus redaction, trust, and truncation narrowing, but leaves decision precedence, transition authority, retention, and purge behavior unspecified.
items.title: Investigation evidence state policy is incomplete

items.impact: The enumerated isolation boundary prevents account-state leakage through provider profile mechanisms.
items.statement: AI-059 explicitly forbids sharing authentication, cooldown, usage, history, cache, and telemetry state between account profiles.
items.title: Provider profile isolation is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: - PM-managed overlays may be shared only when the provider/runtime contract explicitly allows safe projection and drift handling.

items.impact: Providers may implement incompatible safety checks, drift detection, revocation, and rollback for instructions, skills, tools, and plugins.
items.statement: AI-060 delegates overlay sharing to provider/runtime contracts without defining a minimum projection, version, drift, revocation, or rollback protocol.
items.title: Overlay sharing lacks a minimum protocol

evidence.exact_quote: - FileManager consumes browser/rendering and terminal/runtime owners instead of re-owning them.

items.impact: The routing rule prevents FileManager from retaining stale visualizer or terminal-action authority.
items.statement: AI-061 clearly makes FileManager a consumer of browser/rendering and terminal/runtime owner contracts.
items.title: FileManager consumer routing is explicit

evidence.exact_quote:
- FinalGUISpec consumes Firecrawl UI disclosure while Tools owns thresholds, billing exceptions, cache/routing disclosure,
  and audit payload semantics.

items.impact: GUI copy and Tools semantics can drift without a shared contract fixture or conformance check.
items.statement: AI-062 assigns Firecrawl disclosure consumption to FinalGUISpec and semantic ownership to Tools, but provides no cross-document schema or acceptance oracle for that handoff.
items.title: Firecrawl UI handoff lacks conformance proof

evidence.exact_quote: - Consumer docs remain consumers and do not own provider semantics unless their owner contract says so.

items.impact: The map keeps wiring, billing, memory, architecture, and external-reference concerns from silently re-owning provider semantics.
items.statement: AI-063 explicitly maps non-GUI web-provider consumers and preserves owner-contract authority over provider semantics.
items.title: Web provider consumer map is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: - Widget_System adds only owner-approved card widget types.

items.impact: Widget type admission can be implemented as an arbitrary local check because the approving owner and approval artifact are undefined here.
items.statement: AI-064 limits Widget_System to owner-approved card types but does not identify the approving owner, request flow, persisted decision, or rejection behavior.
items.title: Widget approval authority is unnamed

evidence.exact_quote: - Consumer repair happens in the same packet as repaired owner docs.

items.impact: Partial owner/consumer updates can be published despite the same-packet rule, leaving implementation-facing contradictions.
items.statement: AI-065 makes consumer drift blocking and requires same-packet repair, but does not define packet identity, atomic validation, partial-failure rollback, or a closure oracle.
items.title: Owner consumer packet atomicity is undefined

evidence.exact_quote: - Log/audit GUI consumers MUST be reconciled in the same packet as repaired owner docs.

items.impact: Stale log/audit labels, fields, or status presentations can remain user-visible while a packet is declared repaired.
items.statement: AI-066 blocks stale log/audit GUI consumers, but does not identify the complete consumer set or define a semantic conformance oracle for reconciliation.
items.title: Log audit GUI drift is not testable

evidence.exact_quote:
- Architecture_Invariants.md remains the owner doc for behavior described by its preserved sections while cross-doc ownership
  follows ContractRefs and boundary notes.

items.impact: Conflicting ContractRefs, boundary notes, or preserved sections have no deterministic adjudication rule, leaving ownership to builder interpretation.
items.statement: AI-067 defines ownership by preserved sections, ContractRefs, and boundary notes but does not specify precedence or conflict resolution among those authorities.
items.title: Owner map conflict precedence is missing

segments.summary: Reviewed AI-039 through AI-044 across legacy identity demotion, runtime/chat boundaries, project activation, degraded indexing, remote activation, and dependency-driven reconciliation; found migration, state-machine, recovery, and ordering-oracle gaps.

Reviewed AI-045 through AI-049 across native workbench lineage, UI/background projections, platform adapters, shared-core ownership, and invalidation policy; confirmed core ownership while finding lineage, race, fallback, and reconciliation gaps.

Reviewed AI-050 through AI-055 across adapter boundaries, typed investigation budgets, install accounting, debug evidence planes, and Debug/Deep Plan overlays; confirmed authority bounds while finding transition, default, accounting, and cross-plane gaps.

Reviewed AI-056 through AI-061 across Debug authority seams, browser evidence, investigation evidence state, provider isolation, overlay projection, and FileManager routing; confirmed profile isolation and consumer routing while finding critical ownership and data-lifecycle gaps.

Reviewed AI-062 through AI-067 across Firecrawl UI ownership, non-GUI consumers, HITL/widgets, owner-first packet repair, log/audit GUI drift, and the owner map; confirmed consumer boundaries while finding conformance, approval, atomicity, and precedence gaps.
